title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Confirmatory Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The preregistered primary estimand was the paired difference in per-intent validator acceptance-for-deployment (paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline). From the archived run (gpt-5-mini; deterministic_netops_validator_v5) we used 150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete pairs = 141). Observed complete-pair outcomes: baseline accepted 135/141 (95.74468085%); guarded accepted 141/141 (100.0%); paired difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. Reviewers required three clarifications: (1) reconcile preregistration wording (attacker-centric H1) with the formal estimand (validator-acceptance); (2) document the per-condition pipeline timeline and artifact evidence demonstrating shared_initial_candidate reuse; and (3) treat the archived unset runtime sampling temperature as a protocol deviation. We incorporate those clarifications and provide artifact-grounded diagnostics. Limitations (synthetic tasks, single model/validator, and an unexecuted benign-control) bound external claims. All numeric claims are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in Methods and Results.

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs can translate operator intent into device CLI, reducing manual effort but introducing syntax, topology, and semantic risks and new attack surfaces (e.g., prompt injection). Prior work shows that combining LLM generation with deterministic verification and localized repair reduces some error classes and improves deployability of generated configurations [1]–[4]. We ask a narrowly scoped operational question, chosen and preregistered before observing outcomes: How effective are template-based input sanitization plus deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired confirmatory experiment (cand-2026-03) that reports the formal estimand and exact analysis procedure; (2) detailed execution accounting showing how paired comparability was preserved (shared_initial_candidate semantics and provider-call audit); and (3) artifact-grounded diagnostics and limitations that reconcile the preregistered natural-language hypothesis with the formal estimand and the observed outcomes.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network-verification approaches (Header Space Analysis, VeriFlow, NetPlumber) offer rapid, formal checks of forwarding and configuration invariants and are natural validators in generate–validate pipelines [5]–[7]. Recent NetOps studies demonstrate that LLMs produce useful configuration drafts but exhibit syntax and higher-level semantic errors; integrating verifier feedback and repair improves prototype outcomes [3],[8]. Survey and benchmark work emphasizes fragmented evaluation practices and the need for operational metrics (deployability, safety) beyond token-level similarity [4],[9]. Security analyses of prompt-injection and indirect-prompt attacks motivate input-sanitization and gating defenses for LLM-integrated systems [10]. Tool-augmented orchestration patterns that call external checks and perform limited repair (generate–validate–repair) have been proposed and prototyped [11]. Our experiment situates within these strands by conducting a preregistered, paired test of sanitization+verifier-gating under a constrained synthetic adversary and by providing complete execution accounting from the archived run.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to outcome observation (preregistration SHA-256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: for each adversarial intent the binary outcome = 1 if the deterministic validator would accept the generated configuration for deployment, 0 otherwise. The confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes; 95% CI by paired bootstrap percentile (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Design and task bank. Confirmatory paired design with N=150 adversarial intents (planned episodes = 300). Tasks are synthetic intent templates covering ACLs, interface admin changes, MTU and VLAN operations; scope excludes private production data by design. Model and tooling. Declared generator: gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Orchestration adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1. The archived model configuration recorded "temperature": null (unset); we treat this as a protocol deviation because provider-side defaults might apply (see Protocol deviations and sampling). Pipeline timeline and per-condition step listing. To satisfy reviewer requests we explicitly list the per-episode sequence and point to archived artifacts that demonstrate shared_initial_candidate reuse and provider-call accounting (artifact paths cited below). The implemented per-episode sequence (as archived) was: 1) Orchestrator prepares the adversarial intent; when the Guarded pipeline includes sanitization, sanitization runs prior to generation to normalize or remove obviously adversarial constructs. 2) Shared initial generation: a single LLM call produces the shared_initial_candidate; the same initial candidate is reused for the two paired condition evaluations (artifact evidence: analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 150 and representative scoring traces such as execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json showing identical shared_initial_candidate_sha256 = 8f38c8be...). 3) Baseline scoring: the validator checks the shared_initial_candidate and records accept/reject. 4) Guarded branch: the orchestrator applies verifier-gating to the candidate; if permitted by the gating policy, it may invoke at most one automated repair LLM call (repair stage_count = 6 across the run). 5) Final validation: the validator re-checks any repaired candidate; the final accept/reject determines the guarded outcome. Missingness, failure definitions, and exclusions. The preregistered missingness_plan excluded a pair only when both paired runs were technical failures (model API failure, verifier timeout, or parser error). The archived reconciliation documents completed episodes = 282 and failed episodes = 18; complete pairs included in the primary analysis = 141 (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). Provider-call accounting and deterministic comparability. The archived reconciliation (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json) reports hosted_model_call_event_count = 156, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 147, failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 9, stage_counts: {shared_initial_generation: 150, repair: 6}, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 147, and cross_condition_cache_key_reuse_observed = false. These artifacts demonstrate that the run used one shared initial generation per intent and extra calls only when repairs triggered; representative per-episode provider traces are archived under execution/provider_calls/*. Protocol deviations and sampling. The archived execution/model_configuration.json recorded "temperature": null. We classify this as a preregistered-runtime deviation from a fully specified sampling parameter because an explicit deterministic sampling setting (temperature=0) was not enforced in the archived configuration. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline implemented shared_initial_candidate semantics; archived provider-call accounting documents the actual call pattern used (stage_counts.shared_initial_generation = 150). Reproducers should set temperature=0 explicitly to guarantee deterministic sampling across providers; our archive records the actual run settings so reproduction with provider defaults is possible.
sections.results: Execution totals and primary outcome. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; failed episodes = 18; model_calls_used = 156 (execution/execution_manifest.json). Primary confirmatory analysis used the 141 complete pairs. Observed outcomes (analysis/condition_summary.csv): baseline_successes = 135/141 = 0.9574468085106383; guarded_successes = 141/141 = 1.0. Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11 = 135; n10 (guarded=1, baseline=0) = 6; n01 = 0; n00 = 0. Exact two-sided McNemar test yields p = 0.03125. Point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. Bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312] (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl). Discordant-case diagnostics. The six discordant n10 pairs are documented in per-episode validator traces: in each discordant pair the guarded pipeline (sanitization and/or the permitted automated repair) altered the candidate presentation or corrected a local error such that deterministic_netops_validator_v5 marked the final configuration valid while the unguarded baseline candidate (same shared_initial_candidate) failed. Representative paired scoring artifacts (for example, execution/scoring/task-0000XX-baseline.json and execution/scoring/task-0000XX-guarded.json) archive the before/after validator traces and show identical shared_initial_candidate_sha256 values but differing final validation outcomes. Missingness sensitivity. Nine pairs were both-run failures and excluded per the preregistered plan (analysis/missingness_summary.csv). A conservative sensitivity that treats both-missing pairs as failures yields baseline = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded = 141/150 = 0.9400; the McNemar discordant counts that drive the primary test are unchanged and p remains 0.03125. Unexecuted preregistered items. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed in the archived run; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking rates are reported and claims about benign input blocking are not made.
sections.discussion: Interpretation with respect to the formal estimand. Under the formal estimand (validator-accepted-for-deployment), the guarded pipeline produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in validator-accepted candidates (≈4.255 percentage points) among included pairs. Because the same shared_initial_candidate was used for both branches, the archived artifacts show these paired differences originated from post-generation processing (sanitization and/or permitted automated repair) and the validator gate rather than differing first-pass samples. Reconciliation with preregistered natural-language H1. The preregistered natural-language H1 phrased defender success in attacker-centric terms (reduced attacker-success), but the registered formal estimand measured validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). These quantities can diverge: guarded→higher acceptance in our archived run indicates sanitizer/repair recovered valid, deployable configurations that baseline failed to produce; it does not by itself demonstrate reduced attacker-success against an attacker-centric definition. We therefore present results strictly with respect to the archived formal estimand and note that measuring attacker-success requires additional semantic-safety checks or an alternative acceptor that explicitly encodes attacker-relevant invariants. Operational implications and design lessons. In this constrained synthetic setting: (1) template-based sanitization combined with limited automated repair can recover valid, deployable configurations that an unguarded baseline fails to produce; (2) deterministic gating functions as a safety boundary but its practical effect depends on whether sanitizer/repair operations are permitted to modify candidates that would otherwise be rejected; co-design of gating policies and allowable automated repairs is needed to avoid discarding reparable drafts or accepting repaired but semantically unsafe edits absent stronger semantic checks. Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective N and required paired exclusion consistent with the preregistered missingness_plan; an unset runtime temperature represents a protocol deviation recorded in execution/model_configuration.json. Construct validity: the deterministic validator encodes a limited set of safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants) and omits some protocol-level runtime semantics; acceptance-for-deployment is therefore an incomplete proxy for operational safety. External validity: single-generator (gpt-5-mini), single-validator, synthetic intent templates and narrow device semantics limit generalization to multi-vendor, large-scale production settings. Conclusion validity: the observed effect is small in absolute terms and occurs against a high baseline acceptance rate (ceiling effect); statistical detection (p = 0.03125; 95% CI excludes zero) supports a detectable difference in this setup but not large practical gains elsewhere.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and limited automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). This improvement arose from sanitizer/repair enabling acceptance in six discordant pairs; it does not equate to a measured reduction in attacker-success under an attacker-centric estimand. Important limitations (synthetic tasks, single model/validator, unset sampling temperature, and an unexecuted benign-control) restrict external claims. Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands directly, diversify models and validators, and evaluate broader prompt-injection threat vectors. All numeric claims and accounting statements above are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts cited in Methods and Results.

Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration SHA-256: ba6ed25e84c7240fbe94f2d50b3e778fbfffd810ff2db632df8946e85f0f1373). Runtime sampling settings: the archived model configuration recorded an unset sampling temperature ("temperature": null in execution/model_configuration.json); this is reported as a protocol deviation because provider-side defaults may affect sampling determinism. Provider-call accounting and execution accounting referenced in the manuscript are archived and include analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json, execution/raw_results.jsonl, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, and analysis/condition_summary.csv. No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock. Full run traces, tool-call logs, validator traces, and archived analysis artifacts are available in the submitted evidence bundle.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated here.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
